rationale: Interpreting the duplication and stale-replay probe. CheckRun fff65ddf030348c59cf8c3f39e26d380 (exit 0, all three cases passed) evaluated all six comparisons and every one holds, with the fault fields reporting that each fault took effect: case B delivered every message addressed to node 2 twice, and case C replaced the leader (node 3 took over), replayed 507 retained messages from the old leader after the heal, and still ended with all three nodes agreeing on the decided values (1,2,3,7,8,9) and following node 3. I append the account with `holds` and no defect judgment, and record the exercised conditions as knowledge. This closes the safety-axis lead opened from the reordering question; the remaining builder work is the actor-layer placeholder-accounting lead, which is the last place my earlier source reading suspected a distinct failure (a shifted index rather than a false arm order) and which I could not construct in the time left this turn.

knowledge.statement: Two faults the captured suites do not exercise preserved agreement and progress in the exercised schedules. With every message addressed to node 2 delivered twice (case B), all three nodes ended with the same decided values (1,2,3,7,8,9) and node 1 still leading. With node 1 cut off from both followers so that node 3 took over, and then 507 messages the old leader had produced while cut off replayed to their receivers after the heal (case C), all three nodes again ended with the same decided values and all of them reported node 3 as the current leader.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, majority quorum, batch_size 1, no snapshots, logical ticks driven by the harness, in-process delivery with transport-level duplication or holding/replay; the harness never inspects or repairs protocol state. Observed endpoints are the decided values and indexes per node and each node's reported leader. One schedule per case, one follower under duplication, and no other fault combined (no reordering in these cases, no crash recovery), so this bounds neither all duplication/holding patterns nor any occurrence rate.

investigations.discriminator: Answered for the exercised schedules (all six predicates held, with the fault fields confirming each fault took effect). No further discriminator is proposed for these two faults; combinations with reordering, crash recovery or partition healing on the new leader would be new questions rather than extensions of this one.

The arm-order account and its tick band are settled. One builder lead remains inside the same layer but with a different mechanism: `unconfirmed_local`'s one-placeholder-per-index assumption in `reconcile_unconfirmed`, where a truncation that arrives before a tick pops the placeholders for entries it discards should leave stale placeholders ahead of a fresh one and shift the index reported to a later caller.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: both faults are answered negatively for the exercised schedules, and the outcome events carry the fields that show each fault actually took effect. Under duplication (case B, `duplicate_to_node2` true) the follower consumed each message twice and the run still ended with all three nodes holding the same decided values and node 1 leading, which matches the source account that a duplicate carries a sequence number the follower has already consumed and is therefore outdated. Under stale replay (case C, `stale_replay` true, `stale_messages_replayed` 507) the two followers took over (node 3), the old leader's retained traffic was delivered after the link was restored, and the run still ended with identical decided values on all three nodes and every node reporting node 3 as the leader - the replaced leader's messages carried a ballot below the survivors' promises and were rejected, and the old leader itself adopted the newer ballot; the entries decided before the takeover (1,2,3), by the new leader during it (7,8) and after it (9) are all decided everywhere. No divergence, no duplicate decision and no stalled node appeared, so no defect judgment follows; the account is bounded to these two schedules and to the endpoint observations listed above.
counterevidence: One schedule per case: the probe cannot distinguish 'the fault was harmless' from 'this particular interleaving made it harmless', and the reported fields only prove the fault was applied, not that every consequential message was actually duplicated or replayed.

In case C the old leader was never isolated from *incoming* traffic, so it learned the new ballot during the same interval in which its own messages were held; a case where the old leader stays ignorant until after the replay is untested.
The duplication case duplicates messages addressed to one follower only; duplication of leader-bound messages (Promise, Accepted, PrepareReq) and of heartbeat traffic is unmeasured.
limitations: Three-node cluster, majority quorum, batch_size 1, no snapshots, no crash recovery and no reordering combined with these faults.
The probe reads decided values, decided indexes and the reported leader per node; it does not read undecided accepted prefixes, per-message counters or the internal ballot state.
Logical ticks are driven by the harness, so timing effects are excluded by construction rather than shown to be irrelevant.
